articles.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or 2026: Who is the English footballer who beat Mbappé, Yamal, and even Messi, ending England’s 25-year wait

articles.body: This might still seem somewhat unbelievable to process, especially for the footballing world that has long worshipped the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, and lately, Kylian Mbappé, but Harry Kane finally did it — he’s the Ballon d'Or winner for 2026. Ending the quarter-century wait for England, Kane has become the first Englishman to claim football's most prestigious individual award since Michael Owen in 2001.In the last few years, people have watched Messi and Mbappé take turns lifting that golden trophy, but Kane walked past them all at the London Palladium this October. And his numbers actually seem unreal when you line them up. 61 goals in 51 appearances for Bayern in one season: these are the kind of stats you’d scribble in a school notebook, not expect from a real person. He powered Bayern Munich straight to the Bundesliga title, picked up the DFB-Pokal, and didn’t miss a step for England. The total? Seventy-three goals across club and country. And at the World Cup, he bagged six more, like it was just a regular day in the office.For Kane, finally winning the Ballon d’Or is almost poetic. Remember, he spent years being celebrated for his goals, but always seemed haunted by the idea that he hadn’t won a major trophy. Tottenham loved him, as he became their all-time leading scorer. England adored him, as he’s the national team’s top marksman.But trophies to speak for his brilliance? Never really enough. Heading to Germany in 2023 flipped the script. He suddenly had a chance to score goals and collect trophies. This moment isn’t just about ending England’s drought; it’s about Kane proving that persistence beats easy glory. He was once a kid released from an academy, shuffled around on loan, and still managed to become one of the world’s most reliable strikers. That’s not luck; it’s sheer grit.Harry Kane: From Chingford to football's biggest stageFor those who are unaware, Kane’s story stretches far beyond stats and medals. Born in Walthamstow, raised in Chingford, he grew up with football stitched into family life. His dad and brother played with him in the park, shaping that competitive instinct from the age of five. He went through Larkswood Primary, then Chingford Foundation School. Ridgeway Rovers was his starting point.Arsenal picked him up young, but let him go at nine, which could’ve ended things right there. Instead, he returned to local football, eventually joining Tottenham’s academy at eleven. His father pushed him to keep playing, and competing against older kids toughened him up. He wasn’t always the biggest, but a late growth spurt changed everything. Kane tried different roles, like midfield and forward, and learned how to connect play, not just finish chances. The versatility he built as a kid still shows in the way he drops deep and orchestrates attacks.The Tottenham years: Grinding and buildingKane’s Tottenham days were a journey in themselves. He didn’t get handed a starting spot. He went on loan to lower-league teams like Leyton Orient and Millwall: real football, rough tackles, jobs on the line. He fought, learned, and came back stronger. His breakout performance at Spurs during the 2014–15 season? 21 Premier League goals. He won Young Player of the Year. Three Golden Boots followed, as he finished as the division's leading scorer in 2015–16, 2016–17 and 2020–21.Kane also shattered Tottenham’s scoring records, finished with a staggering 280 goals, and helped his team reach the Champions League final. But heartbreak lingered as they lost 2–0 to Liverpool, and the trophy cabinet stayed stubbornly empty.Bayern Munich: The move that changed everythingThen came Bayern Munich and with it, everything changed. Kane moved for trophies, not just paydays. He set Bundesliga records right away. Bayern won titles in back-to-back seasons, and Kane became the league’s leading scorer twice. He finally collected a cup winner’s medal. The 2025–26 campaign was his masterpiece: 61 goals, a double-winning year, and those crucial World Cup strikes. Suddenly, his goals didn’t just look impressive; they won things.England captain, record goalscorer, leading the country aheadAway from the club football glories, Kane’s England journey is special in its own right. He scored with his first touch for the national team and eventually became captain. He led England to the World Cup semi-final in 2018, won the Golden Boot, and reached two Euros finals (and yes, suffered gut-wrenching defeats).Even in the latest 2026 FIFA World Cup, England finished in third place after defeating France 6-4 in the third-place playoff match.By October 2026, he’d racked up 91 in 125 England games, tying Peter Shilton’s record for appearances. For all the near-misses and heartbreak, Kane remained the focal point of English football.What does this Ballon d’Or really mean for Harry Kane?For starters, it’s THE badge of honor all players dream about, started by France Football back in 1956. Journalists from around the globe vote based on skill, team success, and sportsmanship. But for Kane, it’s something deeper: proof that perseverance matters more than hype. He fought through rejection, adapted at every turn, broke records, and took a risk moving abroad. Talent took him far, but patience and determination carried him to the summit.And Kane’s story sends a message to anyone feeling overlooked. He wasn’t a superstar kid; Arsenal let him go, Tottenham sent him out on loan. He didn’t lift the Ballon d’Or until he was thirty-three. articles.title: Steven Wright: High School Football: OHSAA announces first round playoff pairings
articles.summary: The postseason has arrived for high school football. The Ohio High School Athletic Association released the first round pairings Sunday, Oct. 25. The top fou...
articles.body:
The postseason has arrived for high school football.

The Ohio High School Athletic Association released the first round pairings Sunday, Oct. 25.

The top four teams in each region receive a bye into the second round. Teams rated fifth through 12th play in the first round on Friday, Oct. 30, with the higher-seeded team designated as playing at home. Home sites are used through the regional semifinals on Nov. 13.

Neutral sites begin with the regional final round on Nov. 20. State semifinals are on Nov. 27. The OHSAA will announce regional pairings at a later date.

State championship weekend will take place Dec. 3-5 at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton.

Here are the first round pairings in each local region. All games are scheduled to be played at 7 p.m. on Friday.

articles.title: WATCH: Dameon Pierce scores TD to reclaim lead for Eagles on MNF
articles.summary: Running back Dameon Pierce gives the lead back to the Eagles against the Cowboys on Monday Night Football with a five-yard touchdown run.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are going back and forth on Monday Night Football. After the Cowboys scored their first touchdown of the night, the Eagles scored their second touchdown to give Philadelphia back the lead at 14-10 early in the second quarter.

Here is a look at Pierce's touchdown, courtesy of the NFL's official social media:

This was a touchdown drive fueled by Dallas' penalties. Early in the drive, the Eagles went for it on fourth and one. Quarterback Tanner McKee fumbled and it was going to be a turnover on downs. However, the Cowboys were offsides, extending the drive for Philadelphia. Later in the drive after the Eagles got into the red zone, Dallas was called for roughing the passer on third down. Pierce scored a touchdown on the next play.

Penalties have been a key part of this game, as the Eagles have yet to get called for a penalty while the Cowboys have six penalties, including a 91-yard kickoff returned for a touchdown that was called back due to a penalty.

articles.title: 📊 Changes at the top and bottom: Brasileirão table after matchweek 32
articles.summary: Two matches wrapped up Round 32 of the 2026 Brasileirão on Monday (26).At Couto Pereira, Grêmio beat Coritiba 1-0 with a stoppage-time goal, ending a seven-m...
articles.body:
Two matches wrapped up Round 32 of the 2026 Brasileirão on Monday (26).

At Couto Pereira, Grêmio beat Coritiba 1-0 with a stoppage-time goal, ending a seven-match winless run.

It was also coach Renato Portaluppi's first win in charge of Grêmio.

Later, Flamengo beat Atlético-MG 3-2 at the Maracanã.

The match featured mistakes by goalkeeper Gabriel Delfim (standing in for Everson for Atlético-MG), a stunning goal from Renan Lodi and late controversy.

In the final play of stoppage time, Léo Pereira went down in the box after a challenge with Renan Lodi.

The referee spotted contact by Atlético's full-back on the Flamengo defender and, without even needing a VAR review, awarded the penalty, which Carrascal converted.

Wednesday (28) - Fluminense vs Internacional

Wednesday (28) - RB Bragantino vs Chapecoense

The day's results brought changes at both ends of the table.

Palmeiras, who had briefly tasted life at the top, saw Flamengo reclaim the lead.

At the bottom, Grêmio's win was not enough to lift them out of the bottom four, but it did push Corinthians deeper into the relegation zone.
